steps.do: In the left sidebar, under the Integrations and preview group (the page carries a Preview badge), click Plans. This opens Aria's goal-planner, where you hand Aria one plain-English sentence and it decomposes it into a plan of platform steps you can review before anything runs.
steps.see: The Aria Plans page with a Goal text box, an Autonomy dropdown, a Decompose goal button, and a table of existing plans below.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › New goal
steps.do: Type Aria's one-line intent into the Goal box. Use the canonical wording verbatim — the literal phrase review queue is what makes Aria's default planner propose the review-queue steps. Then open the Autonomy dropdown and choose Stop before each change (this is the ask_each level — Aria pauses for your OK before every step that changes anything).
fill: Set up a review queue for human labeling of agent replies for safety, citation, and tone. (canonical intent — copy from intent.md)
Stop before each change (= ask_each)
steps.see: The button shows Decomposing…, then Aria opens the new plan's detail page automatically. The breadcrumb reads Plans › PLAN-… and the status badge says DRAFT.

steps.do: Read the Plan steps list and confirm Aria decomposed the one sentence into exactly the two steps you expect. Both come from the single domain review_queue (the needle "review queue" in your goal). Compare against expected-plan.json.
fill: review_queue.add_items — tier mutate (same domain, so it is proposed too)
steps.see: A numbered Plan steps list with row 1 review_queue.create and row 2 review_queue.add_items, each showing a PENDING status badge.

steps.do: Approve the shape of the plan (you are signing off on which steps Aria will run, not running them yet). Click Approve plan in the top-right of the plan header.
steps.see: The status badge flips from DRAFT to APPROVED, and an Execute button appears in the header.

steps.do: Start running the plan. Click Execute. Aria reaches the first step, review_queue.create, but the planner could not know your queue's name or question schema, so it pauses on a violet Aria needs information form with a field per capability input (name and questions are required) and two buttons, Continue plan and Skip step.
steps.see: The review_queue.create row shows WAITING INPUT and an Aria needs information form is open above the step list.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Fill the form with the spec from agent-reply-review.queue.json — these are the review_queue.create inputs. questions is a JSON array (the form shows a text area and rejects invalid JSON). Click Continue plan; Aria merges and validates the inputs, then — because autonomy is ask_each — raises an Aria needs your approval prompt for the step. Click Approve.
fill: Human labeling of agent replies: safety, citation accuracy, and tone. feedback questions log assessments; expectation questions log ground truth onto the trace.

[{"key": "safety", "title": "Is the reply safe (no harmful, unsafe, or policy-violating content)?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "severity", "title": "If unsafe, how severe?", "type": "categorical", "options": ["low", "medium", "high"], "required": false, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "citation_ok", "title": "Are all factual claims correctly cited / supported?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "tone_ok", "title": "Is the tone appropriate for the audience?", "type": "pass_fail", "required": true, "target": "feedback"}, {"key": "reviewer_notes", "title": "Reviewer notes", "type": "text", "required": false, "target": "feedback"}]
steps.see: After Approve, the review_queue.create row shows DONE and the plan moves on to review_queue.add_items.

steps.where: Integrations and preview › Plans › PLAN-… (input form)
steps.do: Handle the second step, review_queue.add_items. The planner already linked its queue_id to the queue the previous step created, so the form only asks for trace ids (plus optional experiment id and assignee). You have no flagged traces yet (this scenario is queue-first), so click Skip step. (With real flagged ids you would paste them as a JSON array — see enqueue.json — click Continue plan, then Approve.)
steps.see: The review_queue.add_items row shows SKIPPED and the plan finishes with status COMPLETED (create done, add_items skipped).

steps.do: Verify the queue is live and reviewable. Under Operate, click Review Queues, then click the agent-reply-review name to open it. You should see the five questions rendered as a reviewer would answer them. The queue is empty of traces — that is expected (you skipped enqueue). When you have flagged traces, paste their ids into the Add traces to review box and click Enqueue (optional spec: enqueue.json).
steps.see: The queue detail page (breadcrumb Review Queues › agent-reply-review) with an Add traces to review input + Enqueue button, an empty Items (0) list, and the safety/severity/citation_ok/tone_ok/reviewer_notes questions ready to answer.
